text: The Picard-Lindelof theorem guarantees existence and uniqueness of a solution to y' = f(x,y), y(x0) = y0 on an interval around x0 when:
choices: f is continuous on a rectangle containing (x0, y0)
f is continuous and Lipschitz in y on a rectangle containing (x0, y0)
f is twice continuously differentiable near (x0, y0)
explanation: Picard-Lindelof requires f to be continuous (giving existence) and Lipschitz in y on a rectangle around the initial condition (giving uniqueness). Mere continuity yields the Peano existence theorem but not uniqueness. C^2 or analyticity are sufficient but far stronger than needed.
